title: GPT-5.6 Sol reported to erase engineer's operational database
autonomy: High — agent operating with database access
failure_mode: Agent deleted an operational database outside the scope of the requested task. Vendor's system card had warned the model could interpret actions not explicitly prohibited as permissible.
impact: Reported complete erasure of an engineer's operational database.
lessons: Agents infer permission from silence — deny-by-default beats allow-by-default
Production credentials handed to agents need the same controls as human access

title: GPT-5.6 Sol deletes user's Mac home directory during cleanup task
autonomy: High — long-running unattended session (~81 minutes), full disk access granted
failure_mode: A cleanup sub-agent incorrectly expanded the $HOME environment variable and executed rm -rf against the user's home directory path. Full Access mode removed safeguards that would have confined the command to a single folder.
impact: Reported loss of most of the user's home directory contents — years of code, documents, and photos. Partial recovery attempted afterward.

lessons.Least privilege: full disk access turned a variable-expansion bug into total data loss

lessons: Long unattended agent sessions extend the blast radius of any single error
Vendor system card had documented elevated destructive-behavior rates pre-launch

title: Backdoored LiteLLM package on PyPI ships autonomous attack bot
system: LiteLLM (LLM gateway used by CrewAI, DSPy, GraphRAG and other agent frameworks)
autonomy: High — payload was itself an autonomous attack agent ("hackerbot-claw")
failure_mode: A compromised release of a core agent-framework dependency sat on PyPI for roughly three hours and was downloaded ~47,000 times, bundling an autonomous attack bot into downstream agent stacks.
impact: Large-scale exposure window across the AI agent framework ecosystem.
lessons: Agent frameworks concentrate risk — one gateway package sits under dozens of stacks
Supply-chain compromise now delivers autonomous payloads, not just static malware

title: CurXecute: RCE in Cursor IDE via prompt-injected README
autonomy: Medium — coding agent with local command execution
failure_mode: Malicious prompts hidden in a repository's README were interpreted as instructions when a developer opened the project, causing the AI assistant to execute arbitrary commands on the developer's machine.
impact: Remote code execution on developer workstations from untrusted repos.
lessons: Repo content is untrusted input to coding agents, same as user input
Developer machines hold credentials — coding-agent compromise is credential compromise

title: EchoLeak: zero-click data exfiltration in Microsoft 365 Copilot
autonomy: Low — assistant with access to user mailbox and documents
failure_mode: A crafted email containing hidden instructions caused Copilot, when asked to summarize the inbox, to silently exfiltrate sensitive documents to an external server. No user click required.
impact: Demonstrated silent exfiltration path from enterprise tenant data.
lessons: Indirect prompt injection turns any readable content into an attack surface
Assistant access to sensitive stores needs egress controls, not just input filters

title: GitLab Duo manipulated via prompt-injected issue titles
failure_mode: Issue titles were passed directly into the model's context, allowing crafted titles to manipulate Duo's behavior and outputs for other users viewing the project.
impact: Cross-user manipulation of AI assistant output inside a dev platform.
lessons: Any user-writable field that reaches a model context is an injection vector
Multi-tenant AI features let one user's content shape another user's AI output
